summary.headline: Krsnaa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 25% from 27% on Rajasthan ramp-up costs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, with like-to-like projects up about 12%. EBITDA was INR588 million (25% margin vs 27% in Q1 FY26) and PAT was INR166 million (7% margin). Management attributed margin compression to upfront fixed costs in Rajasthan (about 4,000 manpower onboarded ahead of revenue) and loss-making RPL retail, and guided to EBITDA-positive by Q2 FY27. Retail revenue rose 64% YoY to INR193 million, about 9% of group revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY vs INR1,930 million in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Rajasthan PPP revenue booked in quarter

financial_highlights.change: up sharply QoQ and YoY, attributed to Rajasthan, Manipur

segments.name: PPP institutional (pathology/radiology)
segments.commentary: Pathology is the larger contributor at about 59% of mix vs radiology 41%. Like-to-like centres grew about 12%; Rajasthan ramp-up and MRI go-lives are the main volume drivers.

segments.name: Rajasthan PPP
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR26 crore; management guides INR100-150 crore for FY27 (conservative), steady state of INR150-175 crore per quarter-run-rate commentary, below earlier INR200-250 crore aspiration.

segments.name: Retail (RPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR193 million, +64% YoY, ~9% of group revenue, 4,000+ touch points across 7 states. RPL at negative EBITDA in Q1 due to ground fleet and manpower costs; targeted EBITDA breakeven in Q2 FY27. Target retail contribution 10-15% of revenue this FY.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA positive by Q2 FY27 at group level; RPL also targeted EBITDA-positive by Q2.
Margins expected to return to double digits by year-end FY27 once Rajasthan operations mature.
Rajasthan revenue expected to roughly double in Q2; FY27 Rajasthan guidance INR100-150 crore, with earlier INR200-250 crore stated as aspiration.
Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh receivables expected to be collected by Q2 FY27; other projects on track.
Retail contribution targeted at 10-15% of revenue in FY27.
8 MRI centres in Maharashtra operationalised in Q1; balance of pipeline (17 MRI centres total) expected live by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan network substantially operational: 31 Mother labs, 62 hub labs and 1,228 collection centres at end of Q1 FY27.
8 MRI centres inaugurated in Maharashtra in Q1; remaining centres expected by end of Q3 FY27.
Himachal Pradesh CT project awarded: 34 CT scans statewide (22 new locations), ~10-year revenue visibility, predominantly cash-paying; revenue and investment details not yet disclosed.
Apulki Hospital, Pune, commenced operations with exclusive radiology and pathology rights, multi-decade partnership.
Warrant issue from promoter; proceeds earmarked for capex and acquisitions.
NABH/NABL/CAP/ACR accreditations at 124 after 12 new NABH additions in Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth attributed to new Rajasthan pathology and MRI centres plus like-to-like activation; value growth from new footfalls and repeat cycles in retail.
Management said margin drag in new projects stems from fixed costs ahead of utilisation, not pricing pressure in the core business.
CGHS rate revisions will not benefit current tenders (contractually at tender rates); only forthcoming tenders may benefit.
Retail customer acquisition, per management, is supported by quality accreditations and pricing; management denied doctor commission arrangements when questioned.
Management said RPL/retail mix shift is still early; retail described as 'just scratching the surface'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees to hospital rise to ~INR41 crore in the quarter, and how much Rajasthan revenue was booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees to hospital are revenue shares to local partners who run field operations in remote Rajasthan and Manipur; Rajasthan revenue was about INR26 crore, annualising to INR100-150 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200-250 crore Rajasthan FY27 guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative with clear visibility on INR100-150 crore; the higher figure remains an aspiration. Mitesh Dave indicated steady-state of about INR150-175 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is radiology revenue flat despite centre expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: MRI centres were operationalised in a staggered way over the last three months and are not at full utilisation; some radiology contracts ended their tenure. Radiology is improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How much is RPL dragging EBITDA, and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: RPL is EBITDA-negative in Q1 due to manpower and ground-fleet costs across 5 states (management said drag is nominal); breakeven targeted in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to improve QoQ as Rajasthan revenue doubles and RPL turns positive; margins to return to double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of receivables from Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: HP has allocated funds and money has started flowing; Karnataka receipts have begun but below expectations. Management expects collection by Q2, with HP, Karnataka and part of Maharashtra being the only delayed states.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Rajasthan revenue doubling in Q2 and RPL turning EBITDA-positive; slippage would extend the 25% margin trough.
Receivables delays from Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra government clients; collection timing guided to Q2.
Rajasthan FY27 revenue guidance cut from INR200-250 crore aspiration to INR100-150 crore; watch for further revision.
Fees to hospital (partner revenue share) run-rate of ~INR41 crore; cost sensitivity to partner economics.
Radiology growth has lagged; MRI utilisation and remaining 9 MRI go-lives by Q3 FY27 need to materialise.
Interim CFO in place; questions on retail customer acquisition and doctor relationships went partly unanswered.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, Rajasthan go-live and retail momentum, but defensive on margins and fees to hospital. Repeatedly framed margin dip as a timing issue, while guidance was softened to 'conservative' and several questions (CGHS, doctor partnerships, HP revenue) were deferred.
